definition: One of the older generation of Greek gods, children of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Sky), who ruled before the Olympians and were defeated in the Titanomachy.
One of the major gods said to live on Mount Olympus. The canonical list is twelve, though ancient lists vary slightly by place and period.
The food of the Greek gods, said to grant immortality and to keep a divine body from decay. It is usually paired with nectar.
The drink of the Greek gods, poured at divine feasts. Together with ambrosia it is the standard sustenance of the immortals.
The realm of the dead, ruled by Hades and reached by crossing the river Styx. It is not the same as Christian hell, since most of the dead simply lived on there as shadows.
A shrine where a god was believed to answer questions through a priest or priestess. The most famous was Apollo's oracle at Delphi, whose replies were often ambiguous.
Overweening pride or arrogance, especially when a mortal forgets the limits set by the gods. Greek stories often show hubris bringing disaster.
The Greek custom of hospitality, a binding relationship between host and guest that was protected by Zeus. Violating it was a serious religious offence.
A minor female nature deity attached to a particular place or element, such as a spring, a tree, a mountain or the sea.
A large Greek storage jar used for grain, wine or oil. Pandora's container is a pithos, and calling it a box is the result of a much later mistranslation.
